answer: Before earning, a newcomer runs a local kernel check that hashes its seed with a rotating juniper salt, forcing real compute per identity. Participants must stake a bond registered in the atlas, a public ledger mapping each identity to prior work. Duplicating one agent costs a fresh bond plus that work, so mass sybil creation becomes economically irrational while honest peers verify cheaply. In practice, Agent0236 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
